headline: The catalogue runneth over, but not for everyone
standfirst: Four actively exploited entries lead the day: a Zyxel switch overflow carrying a federal remediation clock, a CVSS 9.5 orchestrator flaw that isn't in KEV at all, a CVSS 10.0 Cisco ISE authentication bypass, and a Linux kernel warning that touches everything. Below that, a WordPress XSS that escalates to RCE when an administrator reads a comment, a PhaaS takedown, a DPRK campaign's running total, and malware that no longer needs an operator.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

The lead item is a switch. CISA added a stack-based buffer overflow in Zyxel's GS1900 series to KEV on evidence of active exploitation, and the detail is as unglamorous as it is actionable [[s37]]. CVE-2026-7273 carries a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 and a CWE-121 classification; the description has a LAN-based, unauthenticated attacker sending a crafted HTTP request to the CGI program and potentially executing OS commands, with affected firmware on the GS1900-48HPv2 documented through 2.90(ABTQ.1)C0 and model-specific fixed builds above that. The vector is the part worth internalising: this is not an internet-exposed service. It is an attacker already on your network — a guest VLAN, an unpatched server, a compromised workstation — reaching management-plane hardware that almost nobody instruments. CISA's required action runs through BOD 26-04 with a due date only days after listing. The same report flags Veeam flaws under active exploitation for SYSTEM-level access, which is the more consequential half if you run the backup infrastructure that holds your recovery path.

Do not let the catalogue stand in for your risk register. Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-93952 in on-prem VeloCloud Orchestrator [[s10]], and the enrichment puts it at CVSS 4.0 9.5 — critical, unauthenticated, network-accessible, CWE-20 — yet the KEV lookup returns a confirmed miss. Only orchestrators configured to authenticate their Edges with certificates are affected in the described setup, and hosted versions including dedicated ones were already patched, which narrows the population considerably. But an on-prem orchestrator is the control point for an entire SD-WAN; successful exploitation compromises the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the orchestrator and the data it manages. KEV absence means no federal timeline and no automatic priority bump in a great many ticketing systems. If you are in that certificate-based configuration, you are the remediation deadline.

The two additions in [[s50]] are a study in contrast. CVE-2026-76460 in Cisco Identity Services Engine is a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated remote authentication bypass, arising from insufficient authentication control on an API endpoint (CWE-648) and letting an attacker through the web management interface on ISE 3.1.0 and 3.2.0 builds. ISE is a policy decision point for network access control; a bypass there is a key to the estate. Acronis Backup's CVE-2026-87886 is the quieter one: CVSS 7.8, CWE-276 incorrect default permissions producing local privilege escalation in the cPanel/WHM, Plesk and DirectAdmin backup plugins. Local privilege escalation matters exactly when you are already assuming a foothold — on shared hosting, the isolation boundary between tenants and a backup agent that can read everyone's files is the whole game. Both carry federal due dates that have already lapsed, which tells you the exploitation window opened before most people read the notice.

Then the ubiquitous one. CISA warns that three Linux kernel flaws are being exploited, one of them rated critical [[s41]]. The kernel is the component you cannot meaningfully patch around, and the catalogue entries in that batch show why the effort is still worth it: CVE-2025-39964, a race condition (CWE-362) at CVSS 5.5, and CVE-2026-53266, an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) at CVSS 8.8 in the netfilter bridge's ebtables SNAT ARP rewrite path. Both are marked known exploited, and both carried federal due dates that have already passed. A medium-severity kernel bug in use in the wild outranks a critical one that is not.

## Vulnerabilities

WordPress fixed CVE-2026-93485, dubbed Comment2Shell [[s36]], and the reason it deserves attention is the version range rather than the CVSS. The 7.1 score and CWE-79 label describe an unauthenticated stored XSS, but the affected span runs from 7.1 back through 4.7, and the write-up notes it reproduces on a default install: comment moderation is off by default and the previously-approved-commenter gate can be bypassed. The second stage is the interesting one — an anonymous comment plants a script that runs in an administrator's session and can reach server-side code execution. A confirmed KEV miss is not evidence nobody is using it, and a bug that turns an unauthenticated comment box into a path to the server will be sought out.

## Industry

Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit led a disruption of EvilTokens, a phishing-as-a-service platform whose operators compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts across over 10,000 organisations [[s2]]. PhaaS takedowns are worth reading carefully: removing infrastructure is not the same as removing capability, and the affiliates who rented the kit are still in the business of stealing session tokens. The reason this category keeps working is that token theft does not look like a password attack — no failed logins, no spray, valid sessions from plausible geography. If your detection strategy is built around credential attacks, this is the gap.

## Breaches

A joint advisory puts the North Korean Contagious Interview campaign at a minimum of 30,000 compromised devices across more than 100 countries, with funds and credentials taken from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets and $10.71 million stolen [[s48]]. The target profile — individual web designers, engineers and cryptocurrency specialists — should be read as an acquisition strategy rather than a scattergun: those are the people whose laptops hold repository access, signing material and production credentials. Thirty thousand endpoints is not a campaign you can filter your way out of; it is a population of developer machines that has already been inside the perimeter.

## Research

The most forward-looking item is CLOSEDQUORUM, described as the first reported autonomous AI command-and-control implant and surfaced through a research effort into AI-assisted intrusion [[s28]]. Fully autonomous C2 means the implant no longer waits for an operator to make decisions; portions of the attack chain execute without human involvement. For defenders the practical shift is tempo: human-in-the-loop C2 imposes dwell time, jitter and conversation patterns that detection logic quietly depends on. Strip the operator out and what remains is behavioural — process lineage, beacon regularity, lateral movement that is faster and more consistent than a person would produce. Start calibrating for that now, because the tooling is already here.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

crypto: af_alg - Disallow concurrent writes in af_alg_sendmsg

Issuing two writes to the same af_alg socket is bogus as the
data will be interleaved in an unpredictable fashion.  Furthermore,
concurrent writes may create inconsistencies in the internal
socket state.

Disallow this by adding a new ctx->write field that indiciates
exclusive ownership for writing.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: bridge: make ebt_snat ARP rewrite writable

The ebtables SNAT target keeps the Ethernet source address rewrite
behind skb_ensure_writable(skb, 0).  This is intentional: at the bridge
ebtables hooks the Ethernet header is addressed through
skb_mac_header()/eth_hdr(), while skb->data points at the Ethernet
payload.  Asking skb_ensure_writable() for ETH_HLEN bytes would check
the payload, not the Ethernet header, and would reintroduce the small
packet regression fixed by commit 63137bc5882a.

However, the optional ARP sender hardware address rewrite is different.
It writes through skb_store_bits() at an offset relative to skb->data:

        skb_store_bits(skb, sizeof(struct arphdr), info->mac, ETH_ALEN)

skb_header_pointer() only safely reads the ARP header; it does not make
the later sender hardware address range writable.  If that range is
still held in a nonlinear skb fragment backed by a splice-imported file
page, skb_store_bits() maps the frag page and copies the new MAC address
directly into it.

Ensure the ARP SHA range is writable before reading the ARP header and
before calling skb_store_bits().

alsoCollected.title: New Linux Kernel Flaw Gives ARM64 KVM Guests Read-Write Access to Host Memory
alsoCollected.excerpt: A new flaw in the Linux kernel's KVM virtualization code for ARM64 processors can leave a freed piece of host memory exposed to a guest virtual machine on hosts with nested virtualization enabled. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-89775, allows a guest to read and write host kernel memory, and the researcher who found it says it can be used to escape the guest and run code on the host machine.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: arm64: Handle negative S1 walk levels in VNCR TLB size evaluation

Computing the effects of a TLB invalidation involves looking at
the size of the mapping cached by the TLB. For S1 mappings such as
VNCR, this is deducted from the combination of the base granule size
and the mapping level.

However, this implies that the S1 MMU is *on*. When the MMU is off,
we indicate this with the level being set to a "creative" value of
-127 (S1_MMU_DISABLED).

This ends-up being misinterpreted by pgshift_level_to_ttl() as it
doesn't handle negative levels at all (the level is immediately cast
to a u8 and only the bottom two bits considered), leading to an
invalidation size of 0. Not helpful.

Tidy-up pgshift_level_to_ttl() to handle these negative levels, and
ttl_to_size() to always return SZ_1G when no valid TTL is present.
This allows the removal of open-coded checks for similar situations.

Note that the check for a negative value not explicitely checking for
S1_MMU_DISABLED is deliberate, so that actual negative levels introduced
with LVA2 and D128 can take the same path if we ever support them.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Linux Kernel Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Linux Kernel contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive path which allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass the intended recvmsg() record-type handling, potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
kev.notes: This vulnerability affects an open-source component, third-party library, protocol, or proprietary implementation that could be used by different products. For more information, please see: ; https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/2902c3ebcca52ca845c03182000e8d71d3a5196f; https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/c09dd3773b5950e9cfb6c9b9a5f6e36d06c62677; https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/3439c15ae91a517cf3c650ea15a8987699416ad9; https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/29c0ce3c8cdb6dc5d61139c937f34cb888a6f42e; https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/62708b9452f8eb77513115b17c4f8d1a22ebf843 ; BOD 26-04: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-26-04-prioritizing-security-updates-based-risk ; Forensics Triage Requirements: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-26-04-implementation-guidance-prioritizing-security-updates-based-risk ; https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-39682

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tls: fix handling of zero-length records on the rx_list

Each recvmsg() call must process either
 - only contiguous DATA records (any number of them)
 - one non-DATA record

If the next record has different type than what has already been
processed we break out of the main processing loop. If the record
has already been decrypted (which may be the case for TLS 1.3 where
we don't know type until decryption) we queue the pending record
to the rx_list. Next recvmsg() will pick it up from there.

Queuing the skb to rx_list after zero-copy decrypt is not possible,
since in that case we decrypted directly to the user space buffer,
and we don't have an skb to queue (darg.skb points to the ciphertext
skb for access to metadata like length).

Only data records are allowed zero-copy, and we break the processing
loop after each non-data record. So we should never zero-copy and
then find out that the record type has changed. The corner case
we missed is when the initial record comes from rx_list, and it's
zero length.
